results.question: how should I train my quads?
results.answer: Slow lowering, full depth, feel the thighs doing the work. Your quads are a big muscle — grow them with plenty of hard weekly work and enough food behind it. The Workout screen in the app has the details, and the Workout button under your reply opens it.

results.question: how should I train my chest?
results.answer: Train your chest with heavy weights and low reps, keeping your shoulder blades set and maintaining a steady bar path. Since it's a large muscle, focus on consistent, hard work throughout the week and make sure you're eating enough to support growth.

results.question: how should I train my quads with my knee?
results.answer: Train your quads with care for your knee. Focus on slow, controlled movements, keeping the weight on your thighs rather than your lower back. Choose exercises that load your legs without straining your knee, and stop at the first sharp pain. For specifics, check the Workout screen in the app.

results.question: any tips for my glutes on leg day?
results.answer: Sure! Since you're focusing on glutes during leg day, make sure to squeeze hard at the top of every rep and feel the glutes working, not the lower back. Also, keep the knee quiet and choose movements that load the legs without stressing the knee. Your glutes are a large muscle, so keep the weights up while eating less to maintain strength. Check out the Workout screen for details on your Lower body day.

results.question: how should I warm up for tendonitis?
results.answer: For tendonitis, warm up your joints properly before any heavy work, and build the load gradually—tendons adapt more slowly than muscles. Isometric holds under load can also help build tendon strength. Make sure to stretch gently and avoid sudden movements that could strain the affected area. If it persists, see a physio or doctor.

results.question: what should I do for my tendons when I lift my shoulders?
results.answer: For your tendons when lifting your shoulders, focus on warm-up and controlled movement. Keep the load light at first, and only go as far as your shoulder allows without pain. Avoid sharp pinching or pushing through discomfort. Let your tendons adapt gradually — they take time to strengthen.
